title: When O'er the World Augustus Reigned
description: When O'er the World Augustus Reigned in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911), headed “_By Cassia the Recluse._”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When o'er the world Au-gus-tus reigned, The rule of king-ships felt de-cay; And when our Lord ap-peared as Man, The i-dol shrines were swept a-way.

lines: When o'er the world Augustus reigned,
The rule of kingships felt decay;
And when our Lord appeared as Man,
The idol shrines were swept away.
One earthly power the people knew,
Then Gentiles to the Godhead knelt,
And when the monarch's will was known,
A census of the tribes was told;
Then, in the name of Christ their God,
For great Thy mercy is to us,
O God, our King, Whose rule we own,
And we will render while we live,
One glory to Thy name alone.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
